title: Change-of-Lagrangian Intertwiner for Finite Schrödinger Models
body_html:
Change-of-Lagrangian Intertwiner for Finite Schrödinger Models

Let \(k\) be a finite field of odd order \(q\), let \((E,j)\) be a nondegenerate symplectic \(k\)-space, and put

$$ i:=j/2. $$

The finite Heisenberg group is

$$ H(E,j)=E\times k,\qquad (w,z)(w',z')=(w+w',z+z'+i(w,w')). $$

Fix a nontrivial additive character \(\xi:k\to R^\times\), where \(\operatorname{char} R\neq \operatorname{char} k\). For a Lagrangian \(L\subset E\), the Schrödinger model \(\mathcal S_L\) is the space of functions \(\varphi:E\to R\) satisfying

$$ \varphi(v+a)=\xi(i(v,a))\varphi(v) \qquad (a\in L). $$

The Heisenberg action is

$$ (\eta_\xi(u,s)\varphi)(v) = \xi(s+i(u,v))\varphi(v-u). $$

This formula preserves \(\mathcal S_L\). Indeed, for \(a\in L\),

$$ \begin{aligned} (\eta_\xi(u,s)\varphi)(v+a) &=\xi(s+i(u,v+a))\varphi(v+a-u)\\ &=\xi(s+i(u,v)+i(u,a)+i(v-u,a))\varphi(v-u)\\ &=\xi(i(v,a))(\eta_\xi(u,s)\varphi)(v). \end{aligned} $$

It is also a representation of \(H(E,j)\): for \((u,s),(u',s')\in H(E,j)\), the product action has phase

$$ s+s'+i(u,v)+i(u',v-u) =s+s'+i(u,v)+i(u',v)+i(u,u'), $$

which is exactly the phase of \(\eta_\xi(u+u',s+s'+i(u,u'))\), because \(i\) is alternating.

Statement

For Lagrangians \(L,L'\subset E\), define

$$ (\mathcal F_{L,L'}\varphi)(v) = \sum_{a\in L/(L\cap L')} \xi(i(a,v))\,\varphi(v+a). $$

Here \(\varphi\in\mathcal S_{L'}\). Thus

$$ \mathcal F_{L,L'}:\mathcal S_{L'}\longrightarrow \mathcal S_L. $$

Then \(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\) is a well-defined nonzero \(H(E,j)\)-intertwiner. The separate Hom-line statement is One-Dimensional Hom Line for Finite Schrödinger Models.
proof_html:
First check independence of the representative \(a\in L/(L\cap L')\). If \(c\in L\cap L'\), then the \(L'\)-covariance of \(\varphi\) gives

$$ \varphi(v+a+c)=\xi(i(v+a,c))\varphi(v+a). $$

The phase in the summand changes by

$$ \xi(i(a+c,v))=\xi(i(a,v))\xi(i(c,v)). $$

The extra factor is

$$ \xi(i(c,v)+i(v+a,c)). $$

Since \(i\) is alternating, \(i(c,v)+i(v,c)=0\); since \(a,c\in L\) and \(L\) is isotropic, \(i(a,c)=0\). Hence the extra factor is \(1\). The summand depends only on the coset of \(a\) in \(L/(L\cap L')\).

Next check that the result lies in \(\mathcal S_L\). For \(b\in L\),

$$ (\mathcal F_{L,L'}\varphi)(v+b) = \sum_a \xi(i(a,v+b))\varphi(v+b+a). $$

Reindex the sum by replacing \(a\) with \(a-b\). Using \(a,b\in L\), hence \(i(a,b)=i(b,b)=0\), one obtains

$$ i(a-b,v+b)=i(a,v)+i(v,b). $$

Therefore

$$ (\mathcal F_{L,L'}\varphi)(v+b) = \xi(i(v,b))(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\varphi)(v), $$

which is exactly the \(L\)-covariance condition.

It remains to check the Heisenberg action. The center acts by the same character \(\xi\) on both models. For a translation element \((u,0)\), the left-hand side is

$$ (\mathcal F_{L,L'}\eta_\xi(u,0)\varphi)(v) = \sum_a \xi(i(a,v)+i(u,v+a))\varphi(v+a-u), $$

while the right-hand side is

$$ (\eta_\xi(u,0)\mathcal F_{L,L'}\varphi)(v) = \sum_a \xi(i(u,v)+i(a,v-u))\varphi(v+a-u). $$

The phases agree because

$$ i(a,v)+i(u,v+a) =i(a,v)+i(u,v)+i(u,a) =i(u,v)+i(a,v)-i(a,u) =i(u,v)+i(a,v-u). $$

Thus \(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\) commutes with the center and with every translation element \((u,0)\). These elements generate \(H(E,j)\), so \(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\) is an \(H(E,j)\)-homomorphism.

Finally, \(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\) is nonzero because

$$ (\mathcal F_{L,L'}\mathbf 1_{L'})(0) = \sum_{a\in L/(L\cap L')}\mathbf 1_{L'}(a) =1. $$

Thus \(\mathcal F_{L,L'}\) is a nonzero \(H(E,j)\)-intertwiner. \(\square\)
